correctness.rationale: For the signed lag displacement D=(B-1)y-j on branch j, its positive density at x>0 away from branch breakpoints is (B-1-floor(Bx))/(B-1) on (0,1), by counting admissible j. The negative density is its reflection. Integrating to r gives [2(B-1-m)r+m(m+1)/B]/(B-1), m=floor(Br); substituting Br=m+v gives the asserted fractional-part expression. Stationarity and the 2(N-k) ordered pairs at lag k give the exact finite mean. After benchmark subtraction the scaled summand is exactly 1 for Br<=1. Above the threshold, subtracting F from the scaled summand yields r[u-v(1-v)-u^2]/[u^2(u-r)], bounded in magnitude by 2r/u for r<=1/2. With q=floor(log_b(1/r)), the geometric tail beyond q gives the phase, with total approximation error O_b(r+b^{-(N-q)}); the triangular weight costs q(q+1)/(2N)+O_b((q+1)/N). F is continuous including integers; on (m,m+1) it has derivative 2m(u-m-1)/u^3. This is O(u^-2) and tends to zero from the left at positive integers. The composed summands are globally Lipschitz on [0,1] with summable bounds 2b log(b)b^-j, validating their summed right derivative at phase zero; the endpoint match follows by reindexing and F(1)=1. Consequently the phase is continuous and nonconstant. The supplied checker was inspected, not run; the general identities and remainder were independently derived.
residual_risks: Remainder constants are for fixed b and s; nothing here transfers the mean asymptotic to almost-sure second-order behavior.

value.rationale: The exact iid benchmark separates the interval boundary effect from bulk first-order Poisson behavior. The dominant contribution comes from a logarithmically growing range of deterministic lags, while the next scale retains the phase of the lag threshold. That phase is a nonconstant observable mean correction, not a changed convention for pair ordering or the iid subtraction, and it distinguishes this interval model from its circular counterpart.
residual_risks: The expected bias is smaller than typical random fluctuations; no pointwise detection or fluctuation improvement is claimed.
